summary: Trailing silence and incomplete final JSON when re-establishing SSE after iOS connection warm-up behind Apple HTTP proxy
description: Issue summary: Customer reports SSE streaming sessions ending with a trailing silence and an incomplete final JSON object after an iOS client (managed device) reconnects. The client receives a partial JSON payload (closing bracket missing or truncated final text) but the stream does not emit an explicit terminal event. Impact: Customer's app shows 'incomplete' responses for ~5-15% of long-running streams on iOS 15/16 devices behind the Apple HTTP proxy used in their MDM. This affects Generation and Chat endpoints and causes user-visible corruption in message endings. Environment: prod-us-west, customer using our hosted API via SDK v1.12.0, mobile network: corporate Wi-Fi with Apple HTTP proxy/transparent caching. Observed: - Session logs show a short idle period then a socket rebind/hand-off from device path manager. - Edge logs include: "connection: id=sk-8765 partial_close=true late_fin=true" and serving-runtime logs show "stalled-flush: true" for the stream session. - Client-side: SDK reports reconnect, normal resume handshake, then receives no explicit "[DONE]"-like event or end-of-stream marker; final JSON block is truncated. Steps to reproduce (customer-provided): 1) Start a long streaming generation (>120s) on iOS device on corp Wi-Fi. 2) Background the app for ~10s then bring it to foreground. 3) Observe stream reconnect and final payload missing trailing characters. Expected: stream resumes and emits final terminal event or complete JSON. Observed: trailing silence and truncated final object. Additional notes: Issue more frequent when device OS performs a connection warm-up (path negotiation) or when Apple HTTP proxy inserts an intermediary probe. This appears different from standard proxy chunking issues we've seen previously because the connection close code sequence is unusual (delayed FIN coalesced with keepalive).

[edge-2026-03-12T14:02:11Z] x-request-id=7f9c2a session=ss-04f3
[edge-2026-03-12T14:02:12Z] connection: id=ss-04f3 partial_close=true reason=idle_probe_coalesce code=SOCKET_MIGRATE
[serve-2026-03-12T14:02:12Z] stream_id=ss-04f3 stalled-flush=true kvcache-primed=true last-frame-offset=18432

[client-logs] received chunk: "{\"choices\": [{\"text\": \"...and finally we recommend\"}\n\n(EOF)\n"
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: Apple HTTP proxy on managed networks sometimes coalesces an idle-probe FIN with a subsequent TCP migration, which the edge treats as a definitive stream close before the serving-runtime has flushed the trailing buffered tokens. Differences vs known issues: not classic proxy truncation or chunk reordering; here the edge emits partial_close marker and we see a stalled flush rather than an explicit RST. Reproducer verification: Support able to reproduce locally using an iOS device simulator + a transparent proxy that delays ACKs. Correlation: request ids with partial_close show higher incidence when keepalive interval on client > 20s. Temporary mitigation: instruct customer to enable websocket fallback in SDK or set keepalive to 15s. Observed workaround success: websocket fallback avoided truncation in 30 test runs (0/30 truncations).

resolution: Workaround: customer enabled websocket fallback in their app (short-term). Engineering created a canary server-side mitigation (defer terminal emission by 250ms for sessions that match Apple HTTP proxy heuristics). PR opened and canary shows significant reduction. Follow-ups: - Monitor canary for 48h (Liam/Edge team). - Add more robust detection for coalesced FIN patterns and extend test harness to include Apple HTTP proxy behavior (Ingrid). - Postmortem if rollout proceeds to prod to capture metrics and potential regressions.
